questions.question: What property do you use to enable flexbox on a container?
questions.explanation: You enable flexbox by setting 'display: flex;' on the parent container. This makes the container a flex container and its children flex items.

questions.question: What does 'justify-content' control?
options: How items are spaced along the main axis (horizontal by default)
questions.explanation: 'justify-content' controls how items are spaced along the main axis, which is horizontal by default. Common values include flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between, etc.

questions.question: What does 'align-items' control?
options: How items are aligned along the cross axis (vertical by default)
questions.explanation: 'align-items' controls how items are aligned along the cross axis, which is vertical by default. Common values include stretch, flex-start, center, flex-end, baseline.

questions.question: What is the default value of 'flex-direction'?
questions.explanation: The default value of 'flex-direction' is 'row', which means items flow left to right horizontally.

questions.question: What does the 'gap' property do?
options: Adds space around the entire flex container
Adds consistent spacing between flex items
Controls the size of flex items
questions.explanation: The 'gap' property adds consistent spacing between all flex items. It's much easier than using individual margins on each item.

options: Items will be aligned to the left
Items will be centered horizontally in the container
Items will be aligned to the right
questions.explanation: 'justify-content: center;' centers items horizontally along the main axis (which is horizontal by default).

options: Items will stretch to fill the container height
Items will be vertically centered, regardless of their individual heights
Items will align to the top
Items will align to the bottom
questions.explanation: 'align-items: center;' vertically centers items along the cross axis. Items of different heights will all be centered, not stretched.

options: Items will flow left to right (horizontally)
Items will flow top to bottom (vertically stacked)
Items will flow right to left
Items will flow bottom to top
questions.explanation: 'flex-direction: column;' makes items flow top to bottom, creating a vertical stack instead of the default horizontal row.

questions.question: What is the value of 'justify-content' that spreads items with space between them (but no space at the edges)?
questions.explanation: 'space-between' spreads items with equal space between them, but no extra space at the start or end of the container.

options: A navigation bar with items spaced apart, vertically centered, with consistent gaps
A navigation menu with items aligned to the left
questions.explanation: This creates a navigation bar where items are spaced apart (space-between), vertically centered (align-items: center), with 20px gaps between items (gap: 20px).

questions.question: What is the default value of 'align-items'?
questions.explanation: The default value of 'align-items' is 'stretch', which means items stretch to fill the container's height (or width if flex-direction is column).

questions.question: Which flexbox property would you use to reverse the order of items (so the last item appears first)?
questions.explanation: 'flex-direction: row-reverse;' reverses the order of items so they flow right to left (or bottom to top with column-reverse).
